blocks.text: Northbay operations working group memorandum, draft version 3, circulated 2026-06-25 for comments; not signed or approved. Proposed revision: remove reconciliation from the minor-repair exception and allow team leads to authorize closure; active holds would be reviewed after closure. These proposals would simplify workflows but remain discussion items. The circulation list and successful transmission of this draft are not enactment evidence. Reviewers should identify implementation dependencies before a future vote. No approval or effective date is recorded here. Existing signed decisions remain in force.

Northbay Service Review Board, signed 2026-06-20, effective 2026-10-01. From that future date, exception scope will include major repairs, provided the approval register is positive and reconciliation is complete. A new retrospective review procedure will be introduced separately. Before the effective date, the scope of an existing exception is not expanded by the publication of this future decision. Implementation staff may prepare forms but must not use publication date as effective date. Identity and hold conditions will remain unchanged.

Vendor workshop guidance, issued 2026-05-15. To reduce parts inventory backlog, the vendor recommends allowing closure once payment is received and the repair technician signs the service note. The vendor can certify its own workshop activities but has no authority to amend either regional service review board's closure rules. This recommendation is a supplier workflow preference, not a replacement board decision. The guidance contains the word approval to describe technician acceptance of a parts shipment; that acceptance is not an exception authorization in a customer-case register.

Northbay Service Review Board refund-case policy, signed 2026-04-01. Refund cases are eligible for settlement after a financial approver confirms the refund schedule, even when a physical repair packet does not exist. The policy concerns refund processing only and does not apply to repair-case closure. Sharing a customer, invoice or case-management interface does not merge these two scopes. The financial approver must not be interpreted as a duty supervisor merely because both records have an approved status. All example refund records in this manual are illustrative and should not be imported as repair evidence.

Record of Northbay Service Review Board, signed 2026-04-01, effective 2026-04-01 through 2026-12-31. This decision replaces the 2025 closure policy for Northbay repair cases only. A Northbay repair case may be closed if and only if identity verification is complete, there is no active hold, and at least one of the following two routes is satisfied: (a) the routine documentary packet is complete; (b) the exception route described in the annex signed 2026-03-29 is satisfied. Neither an approval email alone nor payment alone suffices. The ordinary route does not require exception approval. Unavailable facts remain unknown, not false. A recorded false condition is distinct from an unavailable record. The rule is exhaustive for the specified cases; there are no other closure routes. This policy is the authority for the evaluation date 2026-07-01. The separate vendor guidance and the draft memo do not modify this decision.
